requirements.title: CHAR arguments are in-range integer I and optional scalar integer constant KIND
requirements.definition: I shall be an integer value in the range of the collating sequence for the specified kind, and KIND, if present, shall be a scalar integer constant expression.

pending.I-integer-in-collating-range: Positive plans use I=0 and I=ICHAR('A') only through conforming references. Out-of-range I is an unnumbered argument restriction and has no diagnostic facet here.
pending.KIND-scalar-integer-constant-expression: Use CHAR(0, KIND=KIND('A')) and compare KIND of the result with KIND('A'); nonconstant or nonscalar KIND is left as source-control only.

requirements.title: CHAR returns one character of the selected or default kind
requirements.definition: The result is character of length one; present KIND selects the character kind, and absent KIND selects default character kind.

pending.result-character-length-one: Check LEN(CHAR(0)) == 1 and LEN(CHAR(ICHAR('A'))) == 1, with an equal-length comparison so blank padding cannot hide failure.
pending.present-KIND-selects-character-kind: Guarded plan: integer, parameter :: ascii = selected_char_kind('ASCII'). If ascii >= 0, exercise CHAR(ICHAR('A'),KIND=ascii), check LEN(result) == 1 and KIND(result) == ascii, and mutate the requested or expected kind so the KIND check is load-bearing. If ascii < 0, the processor provides no ASCII character kind, so this nondefault character-kind facet is not exercised on that processor; default-kind CHAR facets still apply.
pending.absent-KIND-default-character-kind: Check KIND(CHAR(0)) == KIND('A') for default character.

requirements.title: CHAR selects the character at position I of the associated collating sequence
requirements.definition: The result is the character in position I of the collating sequence associated with the specified kind type parameter.

pending.collating-position-result: Use the portable round trip ICHAR(CHAR(0)) == 0 and ICHAR(CHAR(ICHAR('A'))) == ICHAR('A') rather than asserting a processor-dependent glyph such as CHAR(88).

requirements.title: CHAR and ICHAR obey the specified inverse relationships
requirements.definition: ICHAR(CHAR(I,KIND(C))) has value I for every valid I, and CHAR(ICHAR(C),KIND(C)) has value C for any representable character C.

pending.ICHAR-CHAR-integer-roundtrip: For default character C='A', compute i=ICHAR(C), then expect ICHAR(CHAR(i,KIND(C))) == i; include I=0 as a second non-glyph-dependent case.
pending.CHAR-ICHAR-character-roundtrip: Use C='Z' and C='0'; expect CHAR(ICHAR(C),KIND(C)) == C with LEN(C)==1 checked before equality.
